title: Ordered-Field Minimax Statement
body_html:
Ordered-Field Minimax Statement

The finite minimax theorem admits an ordered-field form: if the payoff matrix has entries in an ordered field and the proof is carried out algebraically through finitely many weak linear inequalities, then the value and optimal mixed strategies can be taken over that ordered field.
proof_html:
Use an algebraic proof route for finite minimax, such as the linear-programming or Dantzig route, whose steps are finite systems of weak linear inequalities, pivot operations, and normalizations by positive elements. These operations make sense over any ordered field. The terminal inequalities are precisely the two minimax optimality systems, so the extracted mixed strategies and value lie in the same ordered field as the matrix entries.

References

  • [MFoGT, Chapter 2, Section 2.3, paragraph after the proof of Thm. 2.3.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Ordered-field generalization via finite weak linear inequalities.
